settings.answer: No. A modern paddle is a solid honeycomb core with a fiberglass or carbon fiber face. There are no strings to break or go dead. The parts that wear out are the grip and the edge guard, and I handle both.
settings.question: Do pickleball paddles need stringing?

settings.answer: It depends on your hand, your budget, and how you play, and the honest way to find out is to hit with one. I keep demo paddles for that. Try one for a few days, and if you like it, I order yours. If you already know the model you want, I can order that one for you.
settings.question: Which paddle should I buy?

settings.answer: Overgrip replacement is $5. A replacement grip is $20. Building a grip up to a larger size is $25. Those are the same prices as my tennis racquet grip work.
settings.question: What does grip work cost?

settings.answer: No. Everything is local pickup by appointment in the Kansas City Northland. It keeps the cost down and lets you see the paddle before you pay for it.
settings.question: Do you ship?

settings.answer: Yes. I stock outdoor and indoor balls, overgrips, edge guard tape, and lead tape, and I can order anything else my supplier carries.
settings.question: Can you get balls and accessories?

settings.intro: Pickleball paddles have no strings, so my stringing machine cannot help you. What I can do is help you pick the right paddle, size the grip to your hand, and keep fresh grips and balls in your bag. I stock very little on purpose: try a demo paddle first, and I order the one you want.

settings.step_1_text: Pick a time online. We meet at the QuikTrip at 9600 N Oak Trafficway in Kansas City, or another Northland spot we arrange.
settings.step_2_text: Hit with a demo paddle, or tell me the model you are looking at and I order it through my racquet sports supplier. Grip work is done on my bench.
settings.step_3_text: Pick up your paddle or your finished grip work at our meetup. You pay when it is in your hand.
